# yaesu-ft-991a

> Yaesu FT-991A — HF/VHF/UHF all-mode transceiver with a built-in USB CAT and audio interface

**Vendor:** Yaesu  ·  **class:** [rig](rig-class.md)

Status: **untested** — catalogued from documented sources, not yet proven here.

**Not maintainer-verified**: nobody on this project has run this hardware yet. The two facts are recorded separately on purpose (D-027) — a correct recipe and a tested device are different claims.

## What it is

A Yaesu FT-991A, a single-box HF/50/144/430 MHz all-mode transceiver with a USB port that presents both its CAT control channel and its sound-card audio over one cable, through a Silicon Labs CP2105 dual serial bridge and a built-in USB audio codec.

## What you can do with it

Run every digital mode and log with full computer control: frequency, mode and PTT over CAT, and transmit/receive audio over the same USB cable, with no external interface. Select it as the station's rig and one shared rigctld carries it to WSJT-X, fldigi, JS8Call, Pat and the rest.

## Setup

Attach the radio and switch it on. In the radio's menu, set the CAT RATE and note it (hamlib defaults 1035 to 38400, but the menu is what counts). `hammunition station set --rig yaesu-ft-991a --rig-device /dev/serial/by-id/usb-Silicon_Labs_CP2105_...-if00-port0 --rig-baud <your CAT rate>`, then install `rig-service`. Join `dialout` and log out and back in. See docs/guides/rig-control.md.

## Known problems

The CP2105 presents two serial ports and only one is CAT; the other keys RTS/DTR. They are told apart by the -ifNN- suffix of the /dev/serial/by-id/ path, not by the USB identifier, which is the same for both. A CAT RATE in the radio's menu that does not match --rig-baud reads as a dead or erratic radio rather than an error — the speed in the menu cannot be read from the computer. This entry is untested here: nothing about the radio's behaviour is claimed until the bench has run (D-073 §12).
